title: Plan the product-card documentation
summary: A frontend developer needs to display a product name, current price, and optional original price. The draft contains only a list of URLs.

title: Capture a reproducible HTTP exchange
summary: A reviewer cannot tell whether a response screenshot came from the documented request.

title: Repair a JSON request body
summary: A writer copied a JavaScript object literal into a JSON request editor.

title: Write a defensive fetch example
summary: A sample always calls response.json(), even for DELETE success, and treats every fetch resolution as success.

title: Compare product PUT and PATCH
summary: The draft says both methods accept any subset of product fields.

title: Document collection boundaries
summary: A product-listing page names limit and offset but does not state bounds or sorting behavior.

title: Write a Problem Details guide
summary: The API returns fields named type, title, status, detail, instance, code, and fields, but the draft calls all of them standard RFC members.

title: Write an endpoint reference
summary: A teammate gives you the add-cart-item operation but no prose reference.

title: Verify an order workflow
summary: A tutorial hard-codes every generated identifier and says checkout charges a card.

title: Test ownership rather than token presence
summary: The reference says any bearer token can retrieve any cart.

title: Prove order idempotency
summary: A client lost the response after placing an order and proposes a new key for every retry.

title: Document conditional GET
summary: A client repeatedly downloads an unchanged product representation.

title: Repair an OpenAPI operation
summary: A path parameter is optional and a request body was placed in the query parameter list.

title: Separate presence from null
summary: A writer assumes excluding a field from required makes null valid.

title: Review security requirements
summary: An API defines global bearer security, but public product reads should not require it.

title: Detect example drift
summary: A response example uses quantity 100 while its schema allows 1-99.

title: Explain four GraphQL list types
summary: A schema review confuses empty lists with null lists.

title: Write a query with variables and aliases
summary: A product comparison needs two products without two indistinguishable response keys.

title: Explain partial data
summary: An anonymous query requests both product and me. A developer discards the entire response when errors exists.

title: Write a cursor-pagination loop
summary: A client increments a decoded cursor and changes sorting between pages.

title: Document a GraphQL mutation
summary: A mutation page lists input types but omits state requirements and duplicate behavior.

title: Review an enum change
summary: A proposed release adds PREORDER while an integration treats every unknown availability value as IN_STOCK.

title: Prepare a documentation pull request
summary: A quantity correction was made only in a generated page and the author claims every test passed.

title: Run a portfolio release review
summary: The project is ready to share, but its README claims official marketplace affiliation and production readiness.
